bugs.what: Fully satisfied 'Something in the Reed-Cuts' (killed the fen-eel, looted 'a woven eel-trap charm' as proof) but the eel-trader had no dialogue option left to deliver it — re-visited twice and 'talk to eel-trader' never reappeared. Quest stayed permanently open.
bugs.where: The Eel-Market (Fenmarch)/talk to eel-trader (option missing after obtaining proof)

bugs.what: Attacking the 'gaunt wolf' (flavor text: 'does not move first') triggered 'Lys disapproves,' but the room had ordinary movement exits I could have used to simply leave — exactly as with the visually identical 'ash wolf' at Twin Stones, where Lys explicitly said 'Leave it. It isn't hunting... We can go around.' Nothing told me the gaunt wolf fight was optional too.
bugs.where: Wolf Scrape (Vale of Ash)/attack gaunt wolf with plain sword

bugs.what: Closing epilogue states 'The reeve of Last Light kept the watch shield you gave back,' but no action across the whole playthrough ever returned the shield — it stayed in my pack unused once a mail shirt replaced it as equipped armor. The line asserts something that didn't happen.
bugs.where: ending screen / status epilogue ('How the realm remembers you')

bugs.what: The reeve's central promise thread ('The Barrow Doors': seal after vs. leave open) was preempted off-screen when the priest's blessing opened the doors before I ever reached the throne. At the throne the Hollow King only says 'Leave it however you see fit' — no explicit seal/open choice was ever offered, so the promise I broke never gets a real payoff.
bugs.where: Throne of the Barrow/talk to hollow king ('the barrow doors — seal or open?')

bugs.what: The intro promises menu entries 'marked (free)' that cost no turn, but in ~600 turns no numbered option ever displayed that literal label. Flavor/investigative actions ('get your bearings,' 'read the notice board,' 'listen to the water') all silently consumed a turn.
bugs.where: Village Gate/get your bearings; Last Light Square/read the notice board

bugs.what: The reeve's dialogue kept listing 'decline to promise' as a live topic long after the promise had already been broken (via the priest), with nothing marking it as stale or inert.

Repeated NPC warnings implying a day/night danger cycle ('mind the cairns after dark,' 'give the Weeping Cairn a wide berth after') never once manifested as an observable mechanic — no time-of-day state or consequence was ever visible.
bugs.where: Highward Parade Ground/Sergeant Rook dialogue; The Mound-Warden's House/talk to warden

bugs.what: All four companions (Vell, Tamsin, Brother Osk, Lys) join for free with no stated cost, limit, or tension, and auto-fight every combat alongside the player. Nearly every fight resolved in one or two exchanges, so combat never felt like a real risk once the party filled out.
bugs.where: party recruitment across the Vale/'come with me' dialogue option

bugs.what: 'the true founding record' (obtained at Highward's record-house, read aloud at the moor's oath-stone) and the separately-quested 'Founding Ledger' (Marrowgate's Hall of Ledgers, gated behind 'Penn, the Church, gold, or your own hands') are similarly named and thematically identical; the game never clarifies whether the former can substitute for the throne's 'read the founding ledger aloud' ending, and I ran out of turns before reaching the Hall of Ledgers to check.
bugs.where: The Hollow Throne/ending options ('read the truth aloud')

bugs.what: 'search the X' actions (bone-litter, brush, alcove, clearing water, muster hollow, mildewed shelves, etc.) never once produced a negative outcome, trap, or empty result across dozens of uses in this run — it reads as a strictly dominant, riskless action wherever it's offered.

Perk offers are visibly class-gated (e.g. 'Honeyed Tongue (+2 will checks (envoy))' only ever appeared for my Envoy) but the four one-line class blurbs at character creation give no hint how narrowly specialized the eventual build becomes.

Whether a '(hostile)'-tagged creature requires combat or can simply be walked past is inconsistent and only revealed by easy-to-miss flavor text ('will let you pass if you let it be' vs. 'attacks on sight'); the menu itself looks identical either way, offering 'attack' alongside ordinary movement with no other cue.
bugs.where: Twin Stones vs. Charcoal Ring (Vale of Ash)/room description text

bugs.what: Three separate routes to open Coldpass (3 hollows rested, Regent's Writ via 2 Watch services, Free Companies' word/smugglers' road for 15 gold) all stayed open at once; once I qualified for the free pilgrim-stair route, Captain Vane's 15-gold smugglers'-road offer became permanently moot with no in-fiction acknowledgement that I'd found a better deal.
bugs.where: Camp Gallows/Captain Vane 'the road under Coldpass'; Coldpass Pass Gate

bugs.what: Some carried quest/lore items show a helpful parenthetical use-hint in the status/carrying list (e.g. 'gaunt rib-bone — the hunter might want to see it'), but others clearly meant for a specific NPC turn-in (e.g. 'a woven eel-trap charm') show no such hint, making it hard to tell which loose items still have somewhere to go.

confusions: No visual difference between an 'attack'-only hostile encounter and one that's actually avoidable by simply walking to another exit — I only learned this after the fact from companion reactions.
The 'Something in the Reed-Cuts' quest gave every appearance of being solvable (find creature, kill it, get proof) but had no reachable completion state once the proof was in hand.
The Barrow Doors promise (a whole quest built around it early on) fizzles rather than resolving, because the priest's blessing bypasses the reeve's condition before the throne is ever reached.
Free-cost actions were promised in the rules text but never visibly marked in six hundred turns of menus, so I could never be sure whether an info action would cost me a turn until after picking it.

It was unclear whether keeping the Vale's crown for myself (instead of resting the Hollow King) would put later content out of reach — the game never confirmed this was a safe, non-softlocking choice until the ending screen made clear the story continued fine either way.
suggestions: Add a turn-in dialogue option to the eel-trader as soon as the reed-cuts proof item is obtained.
Either honor the promised '(free)' menu labels on info/lore actions, or stop advertising the mechanic in the rules text.
Prune dialogue topics that have already fired to a dead end (e.g. a promise already broken) instead of leaving them selectable forever.
Give hostile creatures a consistent tag or preview line for 'must fight' vs 'safe to walk past' before the player commits to attacking.
Let the reeve's Barrow Doors promise resolve with an explicit seal/open choice at the throne regardless of how the doors were physically opened.
Clarify in-fiction whether the Wardmoor founding record and the Marrowgate founding ledger are the same evidence or two distinct proofs.
Add occasional risk or an empty/negative result to 'search' actions so it isn't a free, no-cost habit everywhere.
Preview each class's specialty check (might/grace/wits/will) more explicitly at character creation so the long-term build tradeoff is clear upfront.
Have the ending epilogue only assert player actions that were actually taken (double-check lines like 'you gave back the shield' against real inventory state).
Add a small cost or narrative pushback to recruiting a full four-person party so combat retains some tension in the back half of the game.
